en.title: Names that stay fixed
en.story: A desk sign is intended to stay fixed while this small program runs. Its initial value is Open. Predict what the supplied output statement prints, then inspect how your track expresses that intention. Java, JavaScript and TypeScript can prevent reassignment of the binding shown here. Python uses an uppercase naming convention for a value intended as a constant; that convention does not make reassignment fail automatically. The shared goal is to communicate which value should remain fixed, while respecting the different guarantees each language actually provides.
en.idea: A fixed binding is a name you do not reassign during the program's run. Java writes final before its declaration, while JavaScript and TypeScript use const for this example. Python's uppercase SIGN is a convention understood by readers and tools, not a runtime lock. Changing the initializer in source before a new run is different from reassigning the binding later during the same run. Here the value is a string. This lesson concerns whether the name itself may receive a new value; other kinds of change belong to later lessons.
en.make: Change the initializer from Open to Closed, then run the program again. The declaration still communicates a fixed sign during that run. Do not add a second assignment as the solution. The prediction exercise asks you to distinguish changing the source initializer from changing a binding after it has been initialized. In Python, a later reassignment may execute but violates the stated convention; explain that difference instead of expecting an error the language does not guarantee. Use the notes to compare the spelling used by another track.
en.recap: Fixed intent and enforced restrictions are related but different. The supplied Java final and JavaScript or TypeScript const declarations prevent reassignment of this binding. Python's uppercase spelling communicates a convention. A new initializer can choose a different fixed value for the next run without adding a later reassignment. Recall which guarantee your chosen track provides, then compare it with the others. The last lesson in this module returns to numeric values and shows how to convert a string of digits received as text.
